_about: TRANSLATOR SHELF: Eugene Schuyler (1840-1890), American diplomat and scholar, the first to put Turgenev and Tolstoy into English from the Russian: Turgenev's Fathers and Sons (Leypoldt & Holt, New York, 1867) and Tolstoy's The Cossacks (Sampson Low, London, 1878). US public domain. Added 2026-10-23 by lane C (round 121); Adam may veto. No uids minted.
_surname_note: Full name only; bare 'schuyler' is a common American surname.

eugene-schuyler-turgenev-fathers-and-son.scan_edition: Leypoldt & Holt, New York 1867; Google scan of a Harvard copy
eugene-schuyler-turgenev-fathers-and-son.note: The first English translation. Hogarth's Fathers and Sons and Garnett's Fathers and Children are on their own shelves.

eugene-schuyler-tolstoy-the-cossacks.work: The Cossacks: A Tale of the Caucasus in 1852
eugene-schuyler-tolstoy-the-cossacks.scan_edition: Sampson Low, Marston, Searle, & Rivington, London 1878 (preface dated July 9, 1878); Google scan
eugene-schuyler-tolstoy-the-cossacks.note: The Maudes' Cossacks is on the maude shelf.
